Distinguished delegates, civil society organizations stand united in urging ambitious and inclusive action to tackle desertification, land degradation, and drought. Today, we have three demands. First, we call on parties to develop and implement policies and governance frameworks that actively end support for harmful activities such as land-degrading agriculture, extractive industries and deforestation. promote agroecological and agroforestry approaches, support locally led initiatives and traditional knowledge on sustainable land use, conservation and restoration, promote environmental education focused on youth and children, support peace efforts to end conflicts across the world which hinder attempts to tackle DLDD. Those policies are central to building drought resilience, restoring ecosystems, ensuring sustainable use and fostering healthy food systems. Second, provide accessible funding through innovative mechanisms tailored to the needs of rights holders and grassroots organizations, which empower locally led action, knowledge exchange and capacity building. Funding should be made available without political impediments or relying on intermediaries. Finally, we call on parties to strengthen CSO participation for more meaningful engagement including allowing CSOs as silent observers in contact groups, providing financial support for translation services and capacity building, among others. Critical times require critical actions. Thank you, Mr. President, Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, dear friends. As we close this historic COP16, I'm filled with immense gratitude and deep reflection. This COP is not just the conclusion of a meeting. For me, It is the conclusion of a deeply personal journey. Allow me to transport you to the arid landscapes of my childhood for a moment, where drought was not just an occasional episode, but a constant challenge woven into the daily lives of our communities. I remember the resilience of women striving to make the land yield against all odds. the ingenuity of farmers working with nature to survive, and the deep connection we had with our environment. It is from these experiences of resilience that my deep-seated conviction for land restoration emerged, a belief that guided me throughout my professional life. My work with you has been shaped by this bridge between personal conviction and professional pledge between local interventions in my home community and global impact. Mr. President, allow me to first extend my heartfelt thanks to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, its leadership, as well as its people, for its exceptional clairvoyance in hosting this COP. Thank you for the unwavering commitment to elevating the global land restoration and drought resilience agenda. COP16 has been a COP like no other in the 30 years life of the UNCCD, by far the largest, the most inclusive and the most complex conference. And I would like, and I will, and I would add the most beautiful and efficient facility. First, we have elevated the land and drought agenda beyond sector-specific discussions, establishing it as a cornerstone of global efforts to address interconnected challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, food insecurity, migration, and global security. While parties need more time to agree on the best way forward as to how to address the critical issue of drought, I am filled with hope with the launching of the Riyadh Global Drought Resilience Partnership, a landmark initiative to address one of the most pressing challenges of our time. We all welcome the pledges made in that regard by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the 10 members of the Arab Coordination Group amounting to $12.15 billion. We also leave COP16 with a robust ministerial political declaration. It is a powerful testament to our shared ambition and determination, aligned with the United Nations pillars and advancing progress towards sustainable development goals. The 39 important decisions that were adopted by this COP will serve as a guidance not only to all governments in the world, but also to the private sector, indigenous peoples and local communities. Second, this COP has precisely been about people, farmers, pastoralists, indigenous women and youth are at the heart of our efforts to create a more equitable and resilient future. Their voices have guided our work and inspired our collective action. Third, women's rights and secure land tenure has been firmly recognized as central pillars of our work. ensuring that those most impacted by land degradation and drought are further associated with our decision-making processes. To the parties, thank you for giving me the opportunity to serve and work alongside you over the past six years. Your commitment to addressing desertification, land degradation and drought issues have given the space and the authorizing environment to operate. To the entire UNCCD team who worked tirelessly to deliver this COP, thank you for your extraordinary professionalism, passion, and belief in the mission of UNCCD. Delivering this COP was nothing short of a moonshot, a bold and ambitious effort that required exceptional dedication and teamwork. Witnessing your determination, creativity, and commitment throughout this journey has been profoundly inspiring. Your contributions have shaped me and this moment. Their impact will resonate far beyond the perimeter of this scope, leaving a lasting legacy for generations to come. I also would like to extend my heartfelt thanks to all the invisible hands who to me are very visible, but hence including our incredible volunteers, those working tirelessly in the pavilions across this incredible site. My deep appreciation to UN Security officers, to our interpreters, logisticians, editors and translators, and to all service providers who allowed us to operate so efficiently. Mr. President, as I conclude, My thoughts go to the most vulnerable communities. I believe that this COP was not just another UN meeting. It was a call to action. It was a space where discussions and policies laid the groundwork for real, tangible change. But the true measure of our success will not be defined by what we agreed here. but rather by what we did with it. As we leave this COP, the real work begins. With political will, the solutions are within our grasp. The actions we took today will shape not only the future of our planet, but also the lives, livelihoods, and opportunities of those who we know land is the only asset there is. In the name of Allah, the most gracious, the most merciful, and all praise is due to Allah, and may peace and blessing be upon His Messenger. Your Excellencies, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, heads of the members and delegation, honored guests, may peace, mercy, and blessing from Allah to be on you. It's my pleasure to extend a renewed welcome to all of you at the conclusion of the 16th session of the Conference of Parties to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification. On this occasion, I would like to express my heartfelt thanks and appreciation to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz, and His Royal Highness Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Prime Minister. May Allah preserve them for their for their unlimited support in hosting this significant international conference in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Honored guests, this conference witnessed the participation of approximately 75,000 attendees who exchanged views, experiences through more than 600 events held in the blue and green zones. During the conference, the Kingdom launched several initiatives, including early warning initiative for sand and dust storms, the Riyadh Global Partnership to Enhance Resilience Against Drought in 80 of the most drought-prone countries, and the Business for Land Initiative aimed to enhancing private sector participation worldwide in land preservation, combating land degradation, and adopting sustainable land management practices to contribute in achieving the convention of the objectives. Government, private sector entities, and organization also launched numerous initiatives during the conference in this context. I would like to comment the announcement by the Arab Coordination Group of allocating $12 billion to support projects aimed at reducing land degradation and improving drought preparedness. Additionally, nearly 30 decisions were adopted on critical topics, including migration, sand and dust storms, enhancing the role of science, research, and innovation, empowering women to address environmental challenges, and introducing new topics to the agenda, such as rangelands and environmentally sustainable agri-food system. Honored guests, the Kingdom's hosting of this important conference is a continuation of its commitment to environmental issues and sustainable development, reaffirming its ongoing dedication to the collaboration with all parties to preserve ecosystem, enhance international cooperation to combat desertification and land degradation, and address drought. We hope that the outcomes of this session will make a transformative step that strengthen global efforts to preserve land, mitigate degradation, build capacities to combat drought, and contribute to the welfare of societies worldwide. Over the next three years, during the presidency of this conference, the Kingdom will continue its effort to ensure joint international actions. by all relevant parties to tackle environmental challenges, develop innovative solution for land degradation, desertification, and drought, invest in expanding green areas, innovate sustainable solution, share experiences and modern technologies, and adopt initiatives and programs to foster partnership between governments and the private sector, local communities, financial institutions, and non-governmental organization. This includes agreeing and the building tools that enhance joint international efforts. In conclusion, I extend my gratitude to the Executive Secretary of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification and all staff members for their secretariat for their efforts and to ensuring the succession of the session. My thanks also go to all parties to the convention, international and regional organizations, civil society organization and private sector research centers and everyone who contributed to the transformative steps in the history of the convention and its distinction. I would like also to thank all members of the government agencies and the private sector and the civil society organizations in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for active role in making this conference successful. My special thanks to my colleagues in the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture for their continuous and ongoing efforts since the announcement of the Kingdom's hosting this 11. I pray to Allah Almighty to bless our efforts and guide us toward what is good to achieve sustainable development and protect our environment for the future generation. May peace, mercy, and blessing of all of you.

I hereby declare closed the 16th session of the Conference of the Parties of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification.
